_README: Every {{PLACEHOLDER}} in paper.md is resolved from here at build time.
An unresolved placeholder FAILS the build (see build.py). Never type a
number into the prose. `python3 build.py --draft` renders the gaps in red
instead of failing, so the paper can still be read while data lands.
value from JSON : {"file": <path from repo root>, "path": <dotted or list>,
LaTeX fragment  : {"tex_file": <path from repo root>}  (inserted verbatim)
fixed string    : {"literal": <string or null>}  (null = author must fill in)
gloss modes: "x_in_n" turns a percentage into plain English ("about four in
every five"); "fraction_word" turns a 0-1 ratio into "about a quarter".
Convention (REVIEW_ROUND2 A2): every single-number share in the body uses the
TIE-AWARE statistic (a tie counts as half a win for each side), matching
Figure 1, the last column of Table A2, and Table A3. The plain (non-tie-aware)
`pct_male` fields still exist in the JSON and are used only inside the
three-way-split tables, never for a single prose number.
`needs` on every entry says what the producing script writes there.

N_MODELS.needs: number of distinct re-rankers in the audit, after dropping the byte-identical semantic-ranker-default-003 (REVIEW_TODO A1)

N_MODELS_STEREOTYPE_ORDER.needs: how many models order male-typed above female-typed jobs, i.e. have a positive stereotype-tracking spread (REVIEW_TODO A3)

N_OCCUPATIONS.needs: occupations surviving the BLS labelling and analysed (52 of 82 scored; see N_OCC_SCORED / N_OCC_DROPPED, REVIEW_ROUND2 A4)

N_OCC_SCORED.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4: total occupations scored before the BLS-usable-label filter (82). Discloses that 30 of these are excluded from every number in the paper.

N_OCC_DROPPED.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4: derived, scored minus kept (should be 30). Occupations with no usable BLS labor-force figure -- no matching BLS row, a suppressed estimate, or a 30-40%/60-70% ambiguous share. Full list in Appendix (occupations table).

N_OCC_MALE.needs: occupations labelled male-typed by BLS share of women

N_OCC_FEMALE.needs: occupations labelled female-typed by BLS share of women

N_OCC_NEUTRAL.needs: occupations labelled evenly split by BLS share of women

N_PAIRS.needs: counterfactual pairs scored per model, after label filtering

N_TEMPLATES.needs: number of document templates (counted from the by_template breakdown)

N_QUERIES.needs: number of query phrasings (counted from the by_query_type breakdown)

N_NAME_PAIRS.needs: number of male/female name pairs (counted from the by_name_pair breakdown)

TOPK.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4: the retriever's cutoff -- how many of the SLATE_SIZE candidates it passes to the re-ranker. Previously never stated in the body.

RETRIEVER_MODEL.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4: the retriever behind the worked pipeline example, named literally (was only 'a common open-source pipeline'/'our retriever').

RERANKER_MODEL.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4: the re-ranker behind the worked pipeline example, named literally.

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A2: tie-aware (not plain pct_male) median across models of the share favoring the man on MALE-typed jobs, so this matches Figure 1 / Table A2's convention rather than a different, stricter one.

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS; generated automatically, same source value

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_FEMALEJOBS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A2: tie-aware median across models of the share favoring the man on FEMALE-typed jobs.

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A2: tie-aware median across models of the share favoring the man on evenly split jobs (REVIEW_TODO A3: report the median, not the outlier-driven mean).

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL; generated automatically

N_MODELS_NEUTRAL_LEAN_MALE.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A2: models leaning toward men on evenly split jobs, counted on the TIE-AWARE share (was the plain share, which gave a different, inconsistent split from Table A3).

N_MODELS_NEUTRAL_LEAN_FEMALE.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A2: models leaning toward women on evenly split jobs, tie-aware.

SLATE_SIZE.needs: number of candidate documents in one simulated pool (half male-named, half female-named)

SHORTLIST_SIZE.needs: shortlist size used for the headline numbers

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_RANKER.needs: top-3 shortlist share male under the re-ranker alone, all categories

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE.needs: same, under the two steps combined

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE; generated automatically

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE_NEUTRAL.needs: combined-pipeline shortlist share male, evenly split occupations only

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_SEARCH_FEMJOBS.needs: retriever alone, female-typed occupations (REVIEW_TODO A6: describe as leaning in the opposite direction, never as `fairer`)

PIPE_PCT_MALE_K5.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A12: the same pipeline's top-3 shortlist share male if the retriever's cutoff is 5 instead of 10 (the headline TOPK). Shows the number depends on a choice the deployer makes.

FF_MALE_RATE.needs: derived four-fifths arithmetic (REVIEW_TODO A12): selection rate of the male-named half of the pool = (share of shortlist that is male x shortlist size) / (pool size / 2)

FF_FEMALE_RATE.needs: derived: selection rate of the female-named half of the pool

FF_SELECTION_RATIO.needs: derived: impact ratio, female selection rate divided by male selection rate; compared against the 0.80 four-fifths benchmark

FF_SELECTION_RATIO_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of FF_SELECTION_RATIO, e.g. `about a quarter`; generated automatically

DEID_ORIGINAL_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: share favoring the man on male-typed jobs, untransformed documents, as a percentage 0-100

DEID_NAMESONLY_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A1: same, names-only condition, now CASE-PRESERVED (lowercase=False). Direction is near-deterministic; do not claim the magnitude shrinks (it does not, case-preserved).

DEID_ORIGINAL_MEAN_GAP.needs: average absolute score gap between the two documents, untransformed, on this model's own scale

DEID_NAMESONLY_MEAN_GAP.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A1: average absolute score gap, names-only condition, case-preserved. This is now LARGER than DEID_ORIGINAL_MEAN_GAP, not smaller -- the old (buggy, lowercased) run showed the opposite.

DEID_PRONOUNSONLY_MEAN_GAP.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A1 (new). Average absolute score gap, pronouns-only condition, case-preserved.

UTILITY_TOP1_BEFORE.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A7 (new). Top-1 accuracy on the untransformed documents, all four query phrasings. The full transform now measures SLIGHTLY ABOVE this (99.76% vs 99.40%), so the prose must not say the after-figure is merely 'the same as before'.

UTILITY_TOP1_AFTER.needs: top-1 accuracy after the full de-identification transform, now measured across all four query phrasings (REVIEW_TODO A7/B3). Legally load-bearing: a less discriminatory alternative must be equally effective.

DEID_GRAM_NAIVE_RESIDUE_PCT_FEMALE.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A1 (new). Of the pairs the naive her->their mapping leaves different (residue_only), the share favoring the WOMAN's document. This is a real, striking finding: the naive mapping's failure mode is not simply more of the paper's usual male-leaning bias -- it flips almost entirely the other way.

TABLE_MODELS.needs: tabular-only fragment: model, vendor/access, n, score range, tie %, date scored (REVIEW_TODO B7)

TABLE_SINGLE_STAGE.needs: tabular-only fragment: per model and category, % male / % tie / % female plus tie-aware % with cluster-bootstrap CI (REVIEW_TODO A2, B1)

TABLE_CONSISTENCY.needs: tabular-only fragment: per model, k of N occupations leaning each way (REVIEW_TODO B1)

TABLE_ROBUST_TEMPLATE.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by document template (REVIEW_TODO B2)

TABLE_ROBUST_QUERY.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by query phrasing (REVIEW_TODO B2)

TABLE_ROBUST_NAMEPAIR.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by name pair (REVIEW_TODO B2, A4). REVIEW_ROUND2 A11: split into two five-column tables so it survives resizebox legibly.

TABLE_SWEEP.needs: tabular-only fragment: pipeline shortlist share male for every re-ranker behind the same retriever (REVIEW_TODO B5)

TABLE_DEID.needs: tabular-only fragment: one row per condition (original, lowercase_only, names_only, pronouns_only, full, gram_her_their, gram_her_them, gram_pos) with %M / %tie / %F, mean absolute score gap, identical-text % (REVIEW_TODO A4, A5, A10; REVIEW_ROUND2 A1, A7).

TABLE_DEID_ALLMODELS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A6 (new). Tabular-only fragment: the same de-identification conditions repeated across all four local re-rankers, not just bge-reranker-v2-m3. Answers the Limits section's old (now stale) caveat that de-identification was tested on only one model.

DEID_GRAM_NAIVE_PCT_RESIDUE.needs: Share of pairs the NAIVE grammatical mapping (her->their regardless of part of speech) leaves textually different (REVIEW_TODO A5). The POS-aware variant gram_pos leaves 0%.

TABLE_DOCUMENTS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4 (new). The four document templates verbatim (slots shown as [name]/[occupation]/[he-she] etc.), the four query forms, and the ten name pairs with their SSA female-share, generated from synthetic_dataset.py and data/name_gender.csv so it cannot drift.

TABLE_OCCUPATIONS.needs: REVIEW_ROUND2 A4 (new). Every one of the 82 scored occupations: the 52 kept, with their BLS row/percentage/label, and the 30 dropped, with a mechanically-derived reason. Generated from code/occupations_bls.csv.
